report_name: Denmark's National Population Register Breached, 8.8M Records Exposed

threat_actors.name: Unidentified Actor behind CPR Breach
threat_actors.description: An unidentified threat actor that compromised and misused the legitimate credentials of a private company to access and exfiltrate data from Denmark's Central Person Register (CPR). The actor performed a high volume of automated queries over a 10-day period to harvest personal information.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers misused the legitimate credentials of a private company that was authorized to access the Denmark Central Person Register (CPR) system.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: The attackers leveraged the trusted relationship between the Danish government and a third-party private company to circumvent the CPR's direct security and harvest data at scale.

attack_patterns.name: Automated Exfiltration
attack_patterns.description: The threat actors used automated scripts to execute a high volume of queries against the CPR database over a 10-day period to exfiltrate names, addresses, and CPR numbers.

identities.name: Denmark Central Person Register (CPR)
identities.description: Denmark's national population database which was breached, exposing the records of 8.8 million people.

identities.name: Danish Population
identities.description: Approximately 8.8 million current and former residents of Denmark whose personal information, including CPR numbers, was exposed in the data breach.

identities.name: Danish Data Protection Agency
identities.description: The regulatory body that was formally notified of the data breach.

indicators.name: Anomalous High Volume of Queries to CPR System
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous High Volume of Queries to CPR System
id: 7e8b1c2a-3d4e-4f5a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects behavior consistent with automated data harvesting from a sensitive population register API, similar to the 2026 Denmark CPR breach. This rule looks for service accounts making requests to a sensitive search endpoint. In a real environment, this should be implemented as a UEBA rule with thresholding.
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-06
references:
  - https://www.rescana.com/post/denmark-central-person-register-cpr-breach-cyberattack-exposes-data-of-8-8-million-via-company-account-in-2026
tags:
  - attack.t1020
  - attack.exfiltration
level: medium
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/cpr/search'
    c-user|startswith: 'service_account_'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate high-volume batch jobs run by service accounts.
indicators.description: Detects behavior consistent with automated data harvesting from a sensitive population register API, by monitoring for a high volume of queries from service accounts to sensitive endpoints, as described in the hunting hints for the Denmark CPR breach.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous High Volume of Queries to CPR System
